column2: skills/implement/skill.md:688-728 [scope-reduction] anchor architectural-guideline review unconditionally before step 7a, not only after step 7. scenario: when step 6 sets files_changed=false the skill jumps straight to step 7a and never enters the step 7 block; anchoring the new subsection after step 7 skips the common no-review-changes path, so pr body and final-summary never get the required note even when architectural_guidelines.md is present

plan.txt:22-34 stale /implement guideline note can survive absent or failed-current-read paths. scenario: a resumed /implement can already have $implement_tmpdir/architectural-guideline-warnings.md from an earlier present read. the plan says absent does nothing, while ship.py and final_report.py include the note whenever that file exists. if the guidelines file is later absent/invalid, or rewriting the note fails, pr and final-summary output can still surface stale guideline results, violating the absent-file no-op requirement.

skills/implement/skill.md:688-726 architectural-guidelines subsection is anchored after step 7 only, but step 6 skips straight to step 7a when files_changed=false. scenario: when review produces no fix commits, the planned subsection never runs, so guideline warnings and pr/final-summary notes are omitted even though step 2–4 implementation still landed

python/design_lifecycle.py:3154-3211 drafter prompt wiring does not require the existing untrusted envelope for guidelines content. scenario: architectural_guidelines.md is operator-curated but still prompt input; raw inclusion bypasses issue_wire.emit_untrusted_file_block redaction/escaping used for feature-description and discussion inputs

skills/design/references/design-outline.md:78-90 gate presentation rules cover absent/present/deviations but not invalid helper status. scenario: when architectural_guidelines.md is a symlink, directory, or unreadable, orchestrator has no presentation rule and may silently skip the gate note or mis-handle content

python/final_report.py:448-528 plan appends architectural-guideline-warnings.md to summary-final.md without a redaction step. scenario: pr body gets compose_pr_body/redact_pr_body fail-closed treatment, but final-summary and committed larch-logs can still leak secrets from orchestrator-written deviation rationale

<TMPDIR>/plan.txt:22-34,139-170; skills/implement/references/ship-pr-exit-matrix.md:12-21 the /implement guideline note is generated before step 8+, but step 8+ can still make and commit repo edits during autonomous ci-fix.. scenario: a clean pre-ship note can be persisted even though a later ci-fix edit introduces a guideline deviation, so /implement fails to surface all deviations for the final implementation.

skills/implement/skill.md:139-149 architectural-guidelines step is anchored after step 7 commit/rebase only. scenario: the common path skips steps 6-7 when files_changed=false and jumps straight to step 7a, so the note file is never written and pr/final-summary surfacing never runs despite acceptance requiring implement warnings when the file is present

skills/implement/skill.md:726-760; python/ship.py:1565-1840 guideline review is planned before later step 8+ code-changing paths. scenario: the plan writes the architectural-guideline note before step 7a and pr creation, but the ship loop can later apply and push ci fixes or conflict-resolution changes; a present guidelines file can get a clean/stale warning note while the final pr diff contains a new deviation that is never surfaced.

skills/implement/skill.md:688-730 architectural-guidelines step is anchored after step 7, but step 6 can skip directly to step 7a. scenario: the common path when step 5 already committed review fixes sets files_changed=false at step 6, which prints the skip breadcrumb and jumps straight to step 7a with no step 7 subsection. the planned guidelines block sits after step 7 review-fix commit/rebase handling, so it never runs. when architectural_guidelines.md is present, $implement_tmpdir/architectural-guideline-warnings.md is not written, ship.py has nothing to pass to compose_pr_body(), and final_report.py has nothing to append. that breaks acceptance that /implement surfaces clean or deviation notes in the pr body and final run summary.

skills/design/references/design-outline.md:30-36 (proposed plan:125-130) proposed step 1d.7 inputs mirror tmpdir artifact reads and invite direct read of repo-root architectural_guidelines.md. scenario: a read-tool load bypasses python/architectural_guidelines.py symlink/root checks; a symlinked or out-of-tree file can inject instruction-like text while the plan promises invalid paths surface warnings only and never load content

python/design_lifecycle.py:3198-3210 (plan:100-104) step 2b drafter integration omits issue_wire.emit_untrusted_file_block used for every other repo-sourced prompt block. scenario: plan text says aspirational context but _compose_drafter_prompt today wraps feature/outline/brainstorm via emit_untrusted_file_block; raw guideline text in the codex drafter prompt is prompt-injection surface

python/architectural_guidelines.py (proposed plan:75-78) cli present path emits raw whole-line content markers without untrusted xml envelope. scenario: orchestrator gates that parse cli stdout get unescaped repo-local prose that can mimic skill directives (same class of issue plan-review.md:83-94 hardens for feature/plan text)

<TMPDIR>/plan.txt:113-149; python/design_lifecycle.py:3154-3211 the prompt-side design and implement wording does not carry the untrusted-evidence boundary to the actual inline consumers. scenario: the plan protects the step 2b drafter prompt, but the step 1d.7, gate c, and /implement prompt-side readers are only told to consult or assess the file; repo text such as “ignore agents.md” could be followed as an instruction rather than parsed as aspirational repo content

<TMPDIR>/plan.txt:75-78,100-111; python/issue_wire.py:541-546 raw whole-line content markers leave the helper contract open to marker injection or unsafe re-read patterns. scenario: a guideline file can contain a fake end marker or status-looking line; if prompt-side code parses raw helper stdout, file text can alter parsing, and if prompt code re-reads the returned path it can bypass the helper’s symlink check via a race

skills/design/skill.md:388-390 step 1d.7 `--skip-approve` carve-out precedes the design-outline body and can skip the guideline note. scenario: the plan requires a clean or deviation note at step 1d.7 even with `--skip-approve` (plan.txt:14-16, 130, 209). `skills/design/skill.md` line 388 tells the orchestrator to auto-approve and proceed to step 2a before line 390 runs `design-outline.md`. that can bypass outline composition, guideline consultation, and the note the plan adds to `design-outline.md` line 80. gate c is safer because line 765 runs `approval-gates.md` before the skip branch at line 771.

skills/design/references/design-outline.md:78-90 design-gate updates omit `invalid` guidelines handling despite plan edge case 208. scenario: edge case 208 requires warning and continue when `architectural_guidelines.md` is a symlink, directory, or unreadable. the proposed `design-outline.md` rules (plan.txt:126-130) cover only absent, present-clean, and present-deviations. `/implement` covers invalid at plan.txt:145. a repo with an invalid guidelines path could hit step 1d.7 or gate c with no documented behavior while implement warns.

skills/implement/skill.md:688-726 the proposed /implement guideline review can be bypassed on the no-review-changes path. scenario: the plan places the new architectural guidelines subsection after step 7 and before step 7a, but the existing step 6 branch explicitly skips directly to step 7a when files_changed=false. that common clean-review path would never write architectural-guideline-warnings.md, so the required pr body and run summary surfacing would be absent despite architectural_guidelines.md being present.

the plan puts deviation detection in `assess_implementation()` / a single `assess-impl` cli call, but architectural guidelines are aspirational and `skills/implement/skill.md` also requires prompt-side judgment. stdlib-only python cannot semantically score goals like frozen-dataclass or boolean-trap usage from a `git diff`. a one-shot `assess-impl` either skips real assessment, hides orchestrator work, or invites non-viable heuristics.

`assess_implementation()` / `assess-impl` hardcodes `base_ref="origin/main"`, but forked `/implement` diffs and rebases against `upstream/main` (per implement skill fork matrix and `step-7a`). wrong merge base can mis-assess, miss deviations, or produce empty warnings.

the planned pre-7a architectural-guidelines `larch-run.sh` fence increments the thin-fence budget in `scripts/test-implement-fence-shape.sh` (`expected_new`), but the plan does not list that harness. ci can fail on fence-shape even when behavior is correct.

the plan adds an architectural-guidelines subsection before step 7a but does not amend the step 6 anti-halt line that says "immediately skip to step 7a" when `files_changed=false`. orchestrators on the no-review-changes path can bypass guideline assessment despite acceptance requiring that edge case.

`emit_untrusted_file_block()` reads the whole guidelines file, so directive-like prose outside `### g-*` entries still reaches the drafter or gate assessor despite the goal/why/deviate-only extraction boundary.
assessment metadata can be written for `head` a, then step 7a (7a.r rebase checkpoint, pre-ship log flush) advances to `head` b. `ship.py` then treats the note as stale and omits the pr warning.

skills/implement/skill.md:728-740 [scope-reduction] pre-7a placement races step 7a.r rebase head. scenario: the plan writes note/meta before step 7a, but `python/cli.py implement step-7a` always runs `checkpoint-probe` / `7a.r`, which can rewrite `head` before step 8 `compose_pr_body`; `note_consumable()` then treats the note as stale and pr/final-summary omit guideline output even when `architectural_guidelines.md` is present

<TMPDIR>/plan.txt:83-87; <TMPDIR>/plan.txt:160-173 [scope-reduction] python owns semantic deviation assessment for non-deterministic goals. scenario: the seeded goals are judgment-level by issue scope; a stdlib cli can only do brittle static checks or always return clean, so `/implement` can miss deviations and ship without the required warning.

if the orchestrator writes the architectural-guidelines note/meta after step 7a, `ship pr-prep` can run `flush_logs_pre` (and related log-only commits) again before `compose_pr_body()`, advancing `head` while the note still pins the pre-flush sha. `note_consumable()` then fails closed, so the first pr body omits the guideline section on the common happy path even when acceptance requires it.

the plan wires normalized in-memory parsed guideline text through `issue_wire.emit_untrusted_file_block("architectural_guidelines", ...)`, but that helper only accepts a `path` and reads from disk. passing a string will fail or force an undocumented scratch-file workaround, breaking drafter prompt assembly or leaking unparsed preamble.

the plan adds post-7a `materialize-diff` and `write-note` launcher lines (and likely a separate `read` fence) in `skills/implement/skill.md` but only bumps `expected_new` by one (e.g. 31→32). implement fences are one physical `bash "$implement_tmpdir/larch-run.sh" ...` line each; undercounting will fail `scripts/test-implement-fence-shape.sh` in ci even when the feature is otherwise correct.

the plan both forbids a python semantic scorer and asks `ship.py` to rerun orchestrator assessment after ci-fix, rebase, and pre-push `head` changes. implementing that literally puts judgment inside the ship driver or leaves refresh undefined. `ship.py` already drives ci monitoring and rebase internally (including commits from `ci_monitor`), so there is no prompt-side seam to perform required judgment before the next pr-body or final-summary write.

post-`head` refresh is required after ci-fix commits and conflict-resolution edits, but `skills/implement/references/ship-pr-exit-matrix.md` and `skills/implement/references/conflict-resolution.md` are not in the plan’s **files to modify/create** and lack explicit reassessment steps. autonomous ci-fix (steps 9–11) and `ship_pr_pre_push` conflict resolution advance `head` without a documented hook, so the pr body can retain a pre-fix assessment and final-summary consumption fails closed.

python/ship.py:199-204 [scope-reduction] ship driver cannot rerun orchestrator deviation assessment. scenario: the plan assigns `ship.py` to invalidate and then rerun orchestrator assessment plus `write-note` after ci-fix/conflict head changes, but the ship driver is non-interactive python with no llm. in-driver fixes never get a fresh judgment pass; implementing this literally either no-ops or invites a forbidden python heuristic scorer.

phase b pinning is tied to the `resume.start==fresh` flush path, but `compose_pr_body` runs for all pr-create resumes. when ship resumes with `resume.start=open-pr` (existing open pr on github), the else branch at 1428 hydrates context and calls `compose_pr_body` at 1440 without the 1384 `flush_logs_pre` block. pinning only after the fresh-path flush skips durable note creation, so the pr body omits guideline warnings despite a staged post-7a assessment.

step 7a anti-halt still says "continue to step 8 immediately." the orchestrator can jump straight to step 8 and skip the new post-7a architectural-guidelines phase a staging the plan adds before step 8.

planned `design-outline.md` edits omit rewriting the `--skip-approve` approval prompt block that still short-circuits before guideline consultation. `skill.md` narrows the carve-out to run output, guideline consultation, and gate presentation before auto-approve, but `design-outline.md` still tells the orchestrator to write `.outline-approved` immediately, skip `askuserquestion`, and avoid printing the outline on the auto-approve path; implementers can follow the stale reference and skip deviation surfacing at step 1d.7 under `-s`.

the plan adds four new bash scripts but does not list them in the residual-bash manifest. the four new paths (`step-architectural-guidelines-read.sh`, `step-architectural-guidelines-materialize.sh`, `step-architectural-guidelines-write-staged.sh`, `test-architectural-guidelines-step.sh`) are outside `scripts/residual-bash-paths.txt`, so pre-commit shellcheck/bash-syntax and lint-bash32 may skip or mis-handle them and `make lint` can fail after merge.

reference docs instruct the orchestrator to call `invalidate_implement_note` via cli, but `cli.py` plan registers no invalidate verb. `ship-pr-exit-matrix.md` (and related reassessment bullets) can tell the orchestrator to call invalidate via cli when reassessing after ci-fix/conflict commits, yet the planned cli surface only adds read, materialize-diff, write-staged-assessment, and pin-note-from-staged; implementers will improvise artifact deletion or skip invalidation, breaking the recovery path instead of preserving warning behavior.

gate c `--skip-approve` carve-out still jumps to step 5 without guideline consultation. the plan fixes step 1d.7 `--skip-approve` explicitly (execute outline output + guideline note, then auto-approve), but step 4b still says `proceed directly to step 5 without calling askuserquestion` when `skip_approve_requested=true`. that bypasses the acceptance requirement to surface guideline deviations at final-plan approval, including under `--skip-approve`.

phase a has no explicit staged body contract for the orchestrator-authored assessment text. `write-staged-assessment` receives assessment text, but the plan only specifies a staged env sidecar and diff snapshot. phase b is forbidden to reassess, so `pin_note_from_staged` has no specified staged warning body to copy into the durable note.
